title: Big Data — Driver & Truck Performance Analysis
text:
Problem Statement

Primary Question: What insights can help management prioritize which drivers require intervention and which vehicles require inspection, in order to improve fleet reliability and safety?
Specific Business Objective: Identify drivers with a risk factor greater than or equal to 7.0 (on a scale of 1-10) who also have fuel efficiency anomalies, creating a “dual concern” flag for immediate management attention.
Why does it matter?

Gives management a clear, consolidated view of operational risk across 100 drivers
Identifies dangerous driving patterns (speeding, lane departure, unsafe following) before accidents happen
Detects fuel-related mechanical issues through MPG anomalies earlier than maintenance logs
Reduces operational costs through better fuel monitoring, fraud detection, and maintenance management
Provides data-driven risk profiles to support insurance negotiations and premium reductions

title: Big Data — Driver & Truck Performance Analysis
text:
Strategy

Capture the insights in the raw data and match them with the same key fields.
Organize the data through Hive SQL to verify the connections between the tables.
Calculate and define the high-risk drivers through Python.
Detect the anomalies of fuel efficiency by checking the mpg.
Build up a dashboard to view the outcome at once.

title: Big Data — Driver & Truck Performance Analysis
text:
Methodology

Risk scoring approach:

The risk factor combines three components into a comprehensive score from 1 to 10
Formula

Risk Factor = Base Event Risk + Fuel Penalty + Model Penalty = [1 + (events/14) × 7] + [MIN(|z_score|, 2)] + [model_events/89]


Fuel anomaly alerts:

Fuel anomalies are detected using Z-score analysis against each driver’s own 54-month historical baseline
Formula

Z-Score = (Current_MPG - Historical_Mean_MPG) / Historical_Std_Dev
